title: Minimum Deletions to Make Array Beautiful
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, determine the least number of deletions required to make the array beautiful.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, determine the least number of deletions required to make the array beautiful. An array is considered beautiful if its length is even and no two consecutive even-indexed elements are the same. An empty array is deemed beautiful. Deleting elements shifts the remaining elements to the left to fill gaps.
constraints: The final list length must be even.
At every even final index i, values at i and i+1 must differ.
Deletions preserve the order of remaining values, and the empty list is valid.
hints: Build the final sequence from left to right in pairs.
When one value is waiting at an even index, delete every equal next value until a different partner appears.
Append legal values, count rejected equals, then delete one final unmatched value if the kept length is odd.
Keeping the earliest legal partner never hurts later pairings, while an equal partner can never occupy the required odd position.
editorial: Keeping the earliest legal partner never hurts later pairings, while an equal partner can never occupy the required odd position.

tests.explanation: Delete one of the leading equal values to obtain [1,2,3,5], so one deletion is enough.
Two deletions are required to form valid unequal pairs with even length.
